Published online:
    September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (Japan, US, Eurozone, UK, New Zealand, Canada, Singapore, London)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The yen surged ~1.5% to 156.36/USD driven by hawkish BOJ board member Takata signalling an expedited rate hike trajectory, with a September BOJ hike nearly fully priced. Simultaneously, Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish speech last week is pushing markets to price a 61% probability of a Fed September rate hike, limiting USD/JPY downside. Friday's NFP (forecast +56K after July's -23K shock) is the key near-term catalyst — a solid print would further cement Fed hike expectations.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — Fed September hike pricing (61%), NFP outlook, Warsh's hawkish stance, and USD dynamics are all central to the article.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 61% (as explicitly cited by market pricing in the article)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (marginally — only as the alternative scenario if NFP disappoints significantly)
Probability of holding: 39%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — no discussion of Fed cuts whatsoever)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (More hawkish than before) — Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish speech last week shifted market pricing to 61% for a September hike. A solid NFP print on Friday is expected to reinforce that hawkish trajectory further, with strategists flagging supply-side labor constraints (lower immigration, higher retirements) as structural upside risks to payrolls.
